transcript: How did armored French knights drown in the mud at Agincourt? In 1415, King Henry the Fifth faced a much larger French army. Heavy rain had turned the freshly plowed battlefield into thick mud. English archers planted wooden stakes to stop the French cavalry. Armored French fighters struggled as they advanced through the mud. Some drowned in the mud; about six thousand French fighters died overall.
